_expect.name: Harmony Wall Top Rope/ Trad Area

oh_harmony_wall_top_rope_trad_area.blurb: A small dolomite cliff in southwest Ohio's Paint Creek State Park, set beside a walking path below the dam. Of the 21 climbs, most are top ropes, with a few sport lines and a single trad route; some cracks also take gear. Routes are short, roughly 20 to 30 feet. Grades start with easy scrambly 5.2 and 5.3 lines and climb to 5.12, with the biggest cluster around 5.10, so there is something for beginners and for people wanting to push. The stone is mostly solid but some lines are a little dirty, and the wall sits in shade through the day, which suits warm weather. Traffic tends to be light.
oh_harmony_wall_top_rope_trad_area.parking_note: Leave the car in the lot below the dam signed for the Harmony Trail and spillway, close to the restrooms.
oh_harmony_wall_top_rope_trad_area.approach: From the lot, walk past the restrooms and the picnic and playground area; the cliff is about 100 yards along beside the path.

oh_witches_back.blurb: A wooded bouldering zone on the edge of Athens in southeast Ohio, beyond the neighbouring front section. It holds 21 problems on sandstone, running from V0 up to V8, though most fall between about V1 and V4 with a handful of harder lines. Tree cover keeps it shaded, and you can hear and see the nearby highway from the blocks. Several top-outs are sloped and loose, so bring several pads and a spotter. It is one of the denser clusters of problems in the Athens area, and a crack problem here is a standout classic. The walk in is short but steep.

oh_main_rocks.blurb: The principal cliff in a state wildlife preserve in northeast Ohio, tucked in a wooded gorge not far from a waterfall. About 21 climbs are recorded: mostly bolted routes, then top ropes, plus a few boulder problems. Sport and top-rope grades run from around 5.7 to the low 5.12s, with the bulk between 5.8 and 5.11, and the boulders are easy. The sandstone varies, with some loose, blocky sections and some very hard patches, so choose lines with care. Top-rope anchors are bolts, some tucked on the face, and reaching them from a tree is the safer approach. Mosquitoes are heavy in summer.
oh_main_rocks.parking_note: Use the small gravel lot at Lower Dundee Falls, which holds roughly ten cars.
oh_main_rocks.approach: From the lot, cross a field to the creek, ford it on the stone steps and follow the white-blazed Trail B along the gorge for about half a mile to the base.

oh_nature_s_playground.blurb: A cluster of 20 boulder problems in the Geneva Hills of central Ohio, close to the Hocking Hills country. It is the area singled out for newcomers because it is the easiest to reach and has the best stone of the whole hillside. The sandstone is iron-rich and offers sharp crimps. Problems run from V0 to V6, with most in the V0 to V4 range, and there are several friendly low-grade lines such as a few V1s, which makes it a good place to warm up or bring newer boulderers. Shade levels are not recorded, and this is a small, quiet spot rather than a big destination.

oh_island.blurb: A free-standing block of conglomerate sandstone in the Whipps Ledges area of Hinckley, northeast Ohio, standing a short way out from the Main Wall. Around 20 problems and routes circle it: top ropes, a couple of trad lines and boulder problems on its lower side. Rock climbs go from easy scrambles of 5.3 up to about 5.11, while the bouldering ranges from V0 to V5, mostly easy to moderate. Climbs are short, as at the rest of the ledges, which see a mix of sun and shade and busy weekends. Anchors are set up by scrambling to the top, so it suits people comfortable with easy soloing, and the stone is fragile when wet.

oh_christ_died.blurb: One of the named walls at Whipps Ledges, a small sandstone and conglomerate crag near Hinckley in northeast Ohio. It has about 20 climbs, split between top ropes, some boulder problems and a few trad lines such as crack climbs. Grades go from the 5.4 range to 5.11, with most roped climbs from 5.7 to 5.11, and the boulders include some very easy problems and a few much harder ones. Routes are short, roughly 30 feet at the ledges generally. There are several separate boulders nearby, including a large slabby one across from the wall. The rock is fragile, especially when damp, and the ledges are busy on weekends.

ok_east_chandler.blurb: A sector on the east side of Chandler Park, a former quarry area of limestone on the western edge of Tulsa. It is mostly a bouldering zone: of 29 problems, 22 are boulders, with the rest a few sport lines, top ropes and one trad crack. Boulder grades start at V0 and run past V10, covering everything from easy warm-ups to serious projects, while the roped lines run from 5.9 into the low 5.11s. Limestone at the park can be polished and slick, and the park is mostly shaded though summers are hot. The walk from the road is only a minute or so down some steps.
